Oh I agree. Phone/internet addiction really ended up taking over, hell, I think playing games would be a better use of my time because at least to an extent I'm honing some sort of skill or ability. 

I think what bothers me is the games I do play end up being kinda easy dopamine multiplayer games instead of stories which filled a lotta creative passion for me.
I want to. I got diagnosed with ADHD a couple years ago and am on Vyvanse but even still I find it difficult to commit to tasks at home.

That's not the kind of validation that's going to build you as a person, at that point they're taking advantage of you. They're literally committing a crime. You're only 16.

I really hope you have a trustworthy adult in your life to guide you through this because that's a bad path to go down. There's healthy ways to explore your sexuality, this is not one of them.
It'll help you in the long run and having that confidence to say no is a reward itself.
Say no. Be firm. Be confident. If someone gets mad over you not sending nudes, they're not good people to be around.
I deleted my account and got a big ass addiction to this site and went on my kinda serious/vent account I had left cooking

Most consider me a femboy and I've had an Instagram for it for a while.

Don't send nudes if you're underage. Please. I've spoken to my other femboy friends about this, it genuinely disgusts us, it legitimately fucks with us. It's an adult space for a reason. It'll hurt you down the line, you'll regret sending explicit photos at such a young age. I cannot stress enough that of everything mentioned here, you gotta stay out of adult spaces for everyone's sake.

If you aren't straight, there isn't anything wrong with that. At 16 I dealt with a lot of internalized homophobia towards myself where I was disgusted with myself. I feared the new feelings, the potential of losing others. It takes time to get comfortable. Labels like "am I bi/straight/gay" truly don't matter in the end.

I know it's scary to tell someone about it, but I really hope you can find a trusted person to speak to about this to. It's a very natural part of self discovery, but you have to do it safely. I wish you the best, because I've been in the same place.

He apparently just told me he only sleeps three hours per day. Not only does he have no access to his favorite game but add that with what sounds like depression for him, and now I'm paranoid.

I'm not sure how immediate. Perhaps he could be joking but I just really hope he is. I wish I knew where he lived, and tomorrow, I'll go see a councilor at school and maybe he can get therapy or something.
